Moya, J.A. and Pardo, N. (2013). The potential for improvements in energy efficiency and CO2 emissions in the EU27 iron and steel industry under different payback periods. Journal of Cleaner Production 52, 71-83. http://dx.doi.org/10.1016/j.jclepro.2013.02.028

Locators are printed journal page numbers (PDF page = printed - 70). Same JRC EU27 iron and steel model as Pardo & Moya (2013, Energy 54), run for payback periods of 1-16 years; region EU27, base 2010. Main file: Table 1 direct energy (carrier not split, net of process gases) and direct CO2 for 16 process steps plus the works power plant (GJ/MWh; efficiency derived and the printed 32%); EAF electricity 0.481 MWh/t semis and natural gas 0.29 GJ/t semis from Table 1 footnote; Table 6 other operating costs (2010 EUR/t incl. labour and maintenance, energy excluded) as opex-total; 9 BATs with absolute SEC and CO2 derived as Table 1 value plus the Table 3 change (the paper states the savings refer to Table 1), incremental capex and availability year from Table 7; continuous casting capex only; 10 innovative technologies with capex, availability year, state of development and the 85% CCS capture efficiency, plus ULCOWIN (year only). _measures: Table 3 savings with Table 7 investment. _other-values: Table 4 IT changes (relative, not absolute), Table 6 prices, CO2 T&S cost, model 2010 averages (1.87 t CO2 and 15.86 GJ per t crude steel), scaling exponent 0.6, BAT installation counts. Not loaded: Figs 4-7 (charts). Trap: pdftotext prints minus signs as a \x02 control character in some tables.

(1) No price year for investment costs (Table 7); 2013 used and flagged. Prices and other costs are for 2010. (2) See the Pardo & Moya (2013) meta for the list of value differences between the two companion papers (EAF CO2, organic coating, power plant CO2, scrap preheating, oxy-fuel and CCS CO2 changes, pellet plant cost, CO2 T&S cost). (3) Table 1 footnote quotes the EAF per t semis while the table is per t product. (4) Text: "The carbon in the steel reacts with CO and CO2" and "positively charged cathode" (sic). (5) Oxy-fuel burners show a CO2 increase (+0.008) in Table 3.
